metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days post-spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly; reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; apply smoothing or mean-reversion filter to reduce volatility.
- Model underestimates sharp downward corrections (e.g., 34.33, 33.16) after spikes; add a “drop zone” heuristic: if true price drops >5% from peak, forecast must adjust downward by at least 3–5%.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals; apply 1–2 day lag correction for sudden drops or spikes.
- If true outcome shows strong mean-reversion (e.g., 45.93 → 34.33 → 33.16), model should not overreact to short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to anchor forecast.
